The live test grew into six full or partial runs plus labs and three fix batches.

wentPoorly: The decal delivery (MMR-249/259/260/285/290) was built and published before anyone checked that module textures can draw as decals on the campaign map; acc5 found it.
The 'hang' was a native crash hidden by the game's crash reporter failing on a junction; it cost three runs before a WER event was read.
Several agents wrote stray files into the main checkout through relative paths.
One screenshot-review agent looped for 2+ hours on image crops.
wentWell: Labs and bisect launches (decal lab, crash bisect, mesh lab) settled engine questions in 10-40 minutes each instead of full runs.
Reordering world 1 (core first, risky tail last, per-step budgets, relaunch from saves) stopped one hang from losing a whole run.
Parallel fix clusters with disjoint files merged with almost no conflicts.
Static reading of shader sources and the native DLL found the decal atlas limit and the crash site.

risks: Rivers and lake-edge fills read as water but look blocky (hard channel corners, round fill pools); polish not done.
Seasonal snow does not whiten snow regions in winter: the named snow texture never resolves, so the permanentWhite fallback is in use (only land ice and 12-month snow are white).
Whole-world decal totals exceed 5,000 on both worlds (in view about a tenth of the budget); out-of-view cost unmeasured.
Khuzait home terrain is 88% forest (balance pass kept it; a change would alter every world's factions).
The crash fix rests on the binary analysis plus the bisect; any other movable occluder entity added later must be re-created, not moved.
World B has two settlements whose only drawn access is a bridge (6-8 units from a road decal).
content.summary: Map epic 2 sprint 1 is done: the generated campaign map follows FWGC++ end to end and the live acceptance passes all 33 criteria (acc6, siege confirmed in acc6confirm2). Biome terrain, settlements (every city kept, exact 3/2 villages, culture looks, roads to every gate, bridges, ruins), population, climate and magic all ship. Mid-sprint the owner added MMR-288..291 (veins, features, magic water, overlay meshes). The live runs found and fixed three engine-level problems: decals can only use Native's atlas (so veins, rivers and magic water became runtime overlay meshes), the sea paints over blended meshes (magic water uses an alpha-tested depth pass), and moving occluder-carrying entities after a mission crashed the native occlusion rasterizer (now re-created). The increment eaf2863 squashes 142 integration commits onto claude/map-epic-2; nothing is pushed.
